object.title: Conjecture on the adjacency-matrix inequality for graph normalization
object.statement:
Let $A$ be the adjacency matrix of a connected simple graph on $n$ vertices, and let $x\in{\mathbb{R}^{+*}}^n$. Define

$$
y=x\oslash(A+I)x.
$$

**Graph-normalization adjacency inequality conjecture.** The inequality

$$
y^t(A+I)y\leq\lVert y\rVert_1
$$

holds. This is the paper's main conjecture underlying its proposed proof of general convergence: if true, it implies that the $L_1$ norm of the weights increases under normalization and converges, although convergence of the norm alone does not establish convergence of the weight vector.
object.source_name: Laurent Guigues, “Concerning Iterative Graph Normalization and Maximum Weight Independent Sets”, arXiv:2012.07764 (2020).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.07764

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2020).
